about: I help teams turn messy adoption, training, and workflow problems into learning systems people can actually use. My path has moved through defense, enterprise, municipal, SaaS, healthcare, sales, and technical environments, which taught me to design for real constraints instead of ideal conditions.

Before this work, basketball shaped a lot of how I think: prepare seriously, read the room quickly, and keep moving when the play changes. I still bring that athlete's mix of discipline, curiosity, and competitiveness into the systems I build.
I am curious about games, music, visual design, technology, and how hard ideas finally click. I like building work that feels useful, clear, and more alive than a standard document.
capabilities: Translate stakeholder goals and operational priorities into scalable learning strategies
Design role-based onboarding, compliance, and customer enablement journeys
Build AI-assisted QA, content analysis, and skills-alignment workflows
Govern accessible learning assets using Section 508 and WCAG standards
Create scenario-based, simulation-based, and self-paced technical training
Use analytics and support data to identify adoption blockers and reduce escalations

projects.title: Enablement Quest: The Learning Systems Lab
projects.summary: A browser-based RPG-style learning simulation where players investigate workplace performance problems, inspect evidence, talk to stakeholders, and decide whether training is really the right answer.
projects.result: Demonstrates performance consulting judgment through two playable cases: new-hire ramp and stalled sales demo conversion, with earned business-impact canvases and reviewer-facing evidence boundaries.

projects.title: AI & The Future of Work
projects.summary: A RISE 360 microlearning course about how AI is changing work, framed for learners who may be curious, skeptical, or worried about what the technology means for their role.
projects.result: Turns a broad technology topic into a short, approachable learning experience that helps people understand the shift without fear-first messaging.

projects.title: Why Blockchain Actually Matters
projects.summary: A RISE 360 microlearning course that explains blockchain basics and why the technology matters beyond hype or legacy-banking arguments.
projects.result: Makes a complex technical topic easier to understand by connecting blockchain to practical uses, transaction speed, security, and operational efficiency.

projects.title: Don't Get Hooked: A Course on Phishing
projects.summary: A Storyline 360 microlearning course created from a real phishing attempt, designed to make cybersecurity awareness feel immediate and practical.
projects.result: Uses a real-world trigger to help learners recognize phishing behavior and connect security guidance to decisions they actually make.

projects.title: ADDIE Model From Start to Finish
projects.summary: A full instructional design process example for CON 7020, translating technical contracting documentation into a structured online learning experience.
projects.result: Shows analysis, learning-objective mapping, storyboard design, interactive scenario planning, development, and implementation thinking across the full ADDIE process.
projects.detailIntro: CON 7020 is a Defense Acquisition University course focused on Overhead Should Cost Review. The portfolio value here is not the old course link itself; it is the instructional design trail: how dense contracting material became objectives, structure, screens, interactions, checks, and implementation decisions.

detailSections.title: What This Project Shows
detailSections.body: A complete ADDIE workflow: analysis of source content, audience needs, learning-objective mapping, storyboard planning, interaction design, development thinking, review cycles, and implementation considerations.

detailSections.title: Why It Matters
detailSections.body: A recruiter who is not familiar with government contracting can still see the core skill: taking complex technical material and turning it into a learnable experience with structure, sequencing, practice, and clear learner support.

detailSections.title: Artifact Note
detailSections.body: The previously implemented public course link is no longer available, but the course context remains available through the course catalog link.

projects.title: Quality Assurance Review System
projects.summary: A QA commentary workflow for a 50+ screen government eLearning course, documenting structural, instructional, formatting, and compliance issues for the production team.
projects.result: Highlights a systematic review practice across instructional quality, user experience, Section 508/WCAG expectations, and contractual standards.
projects.detailIntro: This project shows quality assurance as a learning-operations practice, not a last-minute spelling check. The work involved reviewing a large eLearning lesson and documenting issues in a way the production team could act on.

detailSections.title: What Was Reviewed
detailSections.body: Course structure, slide flow, learner instructions, interface consistency, visual formatting, feedback clarity, accessibility considerations, and alignment with the expected review standards.

detailSections.title: What It Demonstrates
detailSections.body: The ability to inspect learning assets like a system: find friction, explain the impact, preserve the instructional intent, and give production-ready notes that make revision easier.

detailSections.title: Why It Belongs Here
detailSections.body: QA work is often invisible, but it is one of the places where polished learning experiences are made. This artifact makes that review judgment visible.

projects.title: Job Aid Template System
projects.summary: Performance-support templates created to turn dense regulatory and technical content into clearer job aids for DOD acquisition professionals.
projects.result: Demonstrates information architecture, visual hierarchy, essential-resource curation, and reusable template thinking for on-the-job support.
projects.detailIntro: This project focuses on the part of learning that happens after a course: quick-reference support people can use while doing the job.

detailSections.title: Design Problem
detailSections.body: Dense acquisition and regulatory content needed to become a reusable support format that helped people find the right information faster without reopening an entire course.

detailSections.title: What It Demonstrates
detailSections.body: Information architecture, template design, visual hierarchy, plain-language reduction, and performance-support thinking for technical audiences.

detailSections.title: Portfolio Signal
detailSections.body: It shows that the work is not limited to courses. It also includes tools, references, and systems that support performance in the flow of work.

projects.title: Facilitator Guide Adaptation
projects.summary: A facilitator guide that adapted asynchronous online training into a synchronous instructor-led session using Gagne's Nine Events of Instruction.
projects.result: Shows how the same content can be redesigned across modalities while preserving instructional intent, timing, materials, and facilitation strategy.
projects.detailIntro: This project shows a modality shift: taking training content built for one delivery format and adapting it into an instructor-led facilitation plan.

detailSections.title: What Changed
detailSections.body: The experience needed timing, materials, facilitator notes, learner activities, room/setup considerations, and a sequence an instructor could actually run.

detailSections.title: Instructional Lens
detailSections.body: The guide uses Gagne's Nine Events as a planning structure while keeping the facilitator focused on pacing, learner attention, practice, and transition points.

detailSections.title: Why It Matters
detailSections.body: It demonstrates that the same learning goal can be rebuilt for a different environment without losing instructional logic.
